Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. THE COMPLETE 28-DISTRICT TABLE for the 2022-23 epidemic, from the cleaned PHIM/Ministry of Health national cholera surveillance database (https://cholera.health.gov.mw/surveillance) as extracted by the authors on 20 May 2023; the paper's Figure 1 caption states 'Data were obtained from the Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM), Malawi Ministry of Health (MoH) data on May 20, 2023'. District cases therefore EXCEED the stated national case total by 401 (0.7 percent) while district deaths fall 39 short. The two are not the same snapshot - the district table is a 20 May 2023 extract and the national totals a 30 May 2024 extract - and PHIM evidently cleaned the line list between them. Corroborating evidence that this table is a CLEANED dataset rather than a later cumulative one: Mangochi (8,479 at 12 April 2023 in the OCHA Flash Appeal, metadata index 97), Balaka (4,193 at 17 March 2023, index 95) and Rumphi (1,049 at 17 March 2023, index 95) are all LOWER here than in the real-time daily bulletins, while every other district is higher. The district table is kept as the authoritative final geographic attribution; the 2023 sitrep snapshots already in this file (Index 15-20, 175-193, 201-217) are kept as the within-epidemic trajectory. Each internal row is self-consistent: the printed incidence per 100,000 and CFR reproduce exactly from the cases, deaths and population given. Mzimba is reported here as a single district, not split into the Mzimba North and Mzimba South health districts that PHIM's weekly bulletins use. Lilongwe: 12683 cases, 558 deaths, population 2,626,901. Highest case count and highest death count of any district in the epidemic.

Rows carrying the old 5 (Index 57, 78, 93, 111 and others) are therefore not wrong, they use the narrower definition. The 0.43 percent CFR the bulletin prints is 13/3,013, i.e. facility deaths over all cases - a third definition again. deaths=25 is recorded here as the widest and latest count; CFR is computed as 25/3,013 = 0.83 percent. processing_notes: Source states: 'Mulanje has registered a total of 67 cholera cases since the onset of the rainy season ... He said the district recorded 56 cases for the past week with all patients being treated in the health facilities.' - interpreted as 56 sCh cases. Week approximated as the seven days before the 13 Feb 2024 article (Tuesday-Monday). The two deaths 'of Mozambican origin' are not assigned (unclear whether imported or within the 67). Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. Nested inside the Mulanje 2023/24 season-cumulative row Index 292 (PHIM, 115 confirmed to 26 May 2024) - do not sum with it. [AGENT 2 REVISION 2026-09-30] CONFLICT FOUND LATER BY AGENT 2 (2026-09-30): The Nation, 12 Feb 2024 (metadata 222 pending/see Agent 2 log batch 5) reports the NATIONAL total since 1 Nov 2023 as 67 cases (the same number MANA attributes to Mulanje alone), national weekly counts of about 4 in January 2024 and 7 in the first week of February, and quotes the Mulanje council's latest update as 'two deaths and 13 new cases'. The MANA Mulanje figures (67 total, 56 in one week) are therefore either district suspected-case counts not yet confirmed or a conflation with the national 67. PHIM later confirms 115 Mulanje cases for the season to 26 May 2024 (Index 292), so a large Mulanje flare-up did occur, but the exact February figures are unreliable. Confidence lowered to 0.3. (reason: Agent 2: conflicting national totals for the same weeks (The Nation 12 Feb 2024)) [AGENT 2 REVISION 2026-09-30] CORRECTION BY AGENT 2 (2026-09-30, later the same run): MBC 13 Feb 2024 (metadata 241) quotes the Presidential Task Force co-chair: 'Mulanje has recorded 61 cholera cases, with 9 recorded in the past 24 hours', and MBC 15-16 Feb 2024 report 78 cases within a week and 84 over four weeks (Index 1899). This corroborates a large mid-February Mulanje surge, so The Nation's national '67 since 1 Nov 2023' was evidently stale data rather than evidence against MANA. Residual conflict: PTF 61 vs MANA 67 for about the same date. Confidence restored. (reason: Agent 2: corroboration found (PTF via MBC 13 Feb 2024))

The 1988 refugee-camp epidemics (Mar-May and June 1988; Moren 1991: 951 cases in one camp; Hatch 1994) never entered WHO's national notification, so this is NOT evidence that Jan-Nov 1988 was cholera-free. National total. Written by Agent 3 (redeployed instance, batch 8).
